chunks: Jabir reported from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I sighed in his presence, then said: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, a concern afflicts me without an actual calamity befalling me, or a matter descends upon me such that my family recognizes it on my face and my friend recognizes it.' He said: 'Yes, O Jabir.' I asked: 'What is that, O son of Allah's Messenger?' He said: 'What will you do with it?' I said: 'I love to know it.' He said: 'O Jabir, indeed Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) created the believers from the clay of Paradise and caused their souls to pass through the breeze of Paradise. Thus, the believer is the brother of the believer in terms of his father and mother. So when one of those souls in any of the lands is afflicted by something, these souls grieve for it, because they are of it.'
ai.seo_question: Why do believers feel each other's pain across distances?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) elucidates the metaphysical bond of *al-wala'* among believers, attributing their shared sensitivity to a divine origin where souls were crafted from the essence of Paradise. This hadith, recorded in *Kitab al-Mumin*, underscores the Shia concept of spiritual unity, explaining why a believer intuitively senses the distress of another even without explicit news, reflecting the profound interconnectedness of the faithful community.

en.muhajir-b-ali: : I sighed in the presence of Abu Ja'far (a.s) and said, 'Son of Allah's Messenger, sometimes I feel afflicted for no apparent reason or I am overcome with a condition of grief such that my family and friends see it on my face.' 'Indeed, Jabir,' he replied. 'Why is that, O son of Allah's Messenger? I asked. 'What will you do knowing it?' he asked. 'I would love to know,' I replied. 'O Jabir,' he then said, 'Allah [M.G] created the believers from the earth of Paradise and brought about their souls from the breeze of Paradise. Believers are thus full brothers; so, when one soul amongst this group of souls is afflicted in any place, the rest are depressed, for they are one.’
